poin.isi: Google has open-sourced AX (Apache-2.0), a task orchestrator for AI agents. You declare a job in one manifest file, and the system prepares an isolated sandbox, wires up the repository, and runs it. It is deliberately built to feel like Kubernetes, and today the project hit the front page of Hacker News (Google's repository has around 3,000 stars).

Four things become configurable: the sandbox with CPU and memory limits, a workspace pre-wired to repositories, MCP servers and skill packages, a network gateway limited to an explicit allowlist, and which model the platform uses. Agents can also be paused and resumed, and you can shell into one to watch what it is doing. Honest caveat: Google says the concepts are still changing and major breaking changes are likely before a stable release.

It answers the two questions that always come up before agents touch real work: what exactly can it reach, and who is watching. Because the code is open and can run on your own infrastructure, an agent stops being a black box you simply have to trust.

headline: AI AGENTS NOW GET
AN ENGINE OF THEIR OWN
headline_caption: Google open-sources AX: a clean, isolated and observable way to run AI agents
subjudul: Google opens AX — agents run in isolated sandboxes, networks are allowlisted, and you pick the model.
